step1_figure.description: The provided netlist describes a two-stage Class AB amplifier with a cascode input stage and a wide-swing bias circuit. While the exact full schematic is not drawn in the provided pages, it builds upon the fundamental Class A common-source amplifier shown in Fig 21.17 and is explicitly referenced in the text on page 672 which discusses Class AB operation ('both MOSFETs or a single MOSFET conduct a current at a given time').

slew_rate.description: Maximum rate of change of the output voltage across the load capacitor.

equation.explanation: I is the maximum current the amplifier can source or sink to the output node, and C_L is the load capacitance.
equation.assumptions: Assumes the amplifier's speed is limited by the maximum current of the output stage charging/discharging the load.

sky130_expected.calculation: Assuming a typical Class AB output peak current of 50uA to 100uA and C_L = 1pF, SR = 50uA / 1pF = 50 V/us.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Class AB stages can source significantly more current than their quiescent bias, leading to high slew rates depending on the input step size.

small_signal_gain.description: Low-frequency open-loop voltage gain of the amplifier.

equation.explanation: The product of the input stage transconductance and the equivalent output resistance.
equation.assumptions: Equation 21.39 is for a single stage. For this two-stage cascode + Class AB topology, the total gain is the product of both stages' gains.

sky130_expected.calculation: For SKY130 W/L=10, I_D=20uA: g_m ~ 328uS, r_o ~ 500kOhm. Stage 1 (cascode) gain ~ (g_m*r_o)^2 / 2 ~ 60 dB. Stage 2 (CS) gain ~ g_m*r_o/2 ~ 38 dB. Total gain ~ 98 dB.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Two-stage amplifiers with a cascode first stage typically achieve very high open-loop DC gain in 130nm processes.

unity_gain_frequency.description: The frequency at which the open-loop voltage gain drops to 0 dB.

equation.explanation: Determined by the input transconductance and the dominant compensation/load capacitance.
equation.assumptions: Assumes a single dominant pole response up to the unity-gain frequency.

sky130_expected.calculation: With g_m1 = 328uS and an effective load/compensation capacitance of 1pF: f_un = 328e-6 / (2 * pi * 1e-12) = 52.2 MHz.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Typical bandwidth for a W/L=10 input pair biased at ~20uA driving a 1pF load in SKY130.

dominant_pole.description: The lowest frequency pole that determines the -3dB bandwidth of the amplifier.

equation.explanation: The Miller-multiplied capacitance creates a dominant low-frequency pole at the high-impedance node.
equation.assumptions: Assumes the second stage provides large voltage gain (g_m2 * R_2 >> 1).

sky130_expected.calculation: Assuming total DC gain is 80 dB (10,000 V/V) and f_un is 50 MHz. f_1 = f_un / A_DC = 50e6 / 10000 = 5 kHz.
sky130_expected.reasoning: The extremely high output impedance of the cascode stage pushes the dominant pole to the low kHz range.

step3_testbench.description: Testbench to measure DC operating point (trip point), AC open-loop gain, bandwidth, phase margin, and transient slew rate.
